excerpt: We will publish Risk Reports discussing the risks of our systems and how we have made determinations about whether to continue AI development and deployment in light of the risks.
paraphrase: Anthropic commits to publishing Risk Reports that discuss system risks and the determinations made about continuing AI development and deployment.

excerpt: These have significant content in common with system cards, but we are adding additional structure and process aimed at presenting our overall assessments of risk.
paraphrase: Risk Reports overlap with system cards but include added structure and process for presenting overall risk assessments.

excerpt: A Risk Report will cover all publicly deployed models at the time of its publication.
paraphrase: Each Risk Report covers all models publicly deployed as of its publication date.

excerpt: It will also cover internally deployed models that we determine (1) could pose risks related to high-stakes misalignment or automated R&D that (2) significantly exceed those posed by models covered by a prior Risk Report.
paraphrase: Risk Reports also cover internal models judged to pose materially greater misalignment or automated R&D risk than previously covered models.
stated_bar: significantly exceed those posed by models covered by a prior Risk Report

excerpt: While there are a variety of reasons we might classify an internal model this way, this will—at a minimum—include any internal models that we are deploying for large-scale, fully autonomous research.
paraphrase: At minimum, models deployed internally for large-scale fully autonomous research will be classified as in-scope.

excerpt: Models fitting the above description are abbreviated below as “in-scope models.”
paraphrase: Models meeting the described criteria are referred to as in-scope models.

excerpt: We may also voluntarily include additional models in a Risk Report, e.g., to contribute to general discourse, but such inclusion does not expand the commitments below.
paraphrase: Additional models may be voluntarily included for discourse purposes, without expanding the stated commitments.

excerpt: We will publish a Risk Report every 3-6 months.
paraphrase: Risk Reports will be published every three to six months.

excerpt: Note that unlike system cards, Risk Reports will not be published with each new model release.
paraphrase: Risk Reports differ from system cards in that they are not tied to each new model release.

excerpt: Separate from our publication of Risk Reports, we will publish an analysis of an individual model’s relevant risks (e.g., how the model’s capabilities and propensities affect or change prior analyses) in the following circumstances:
paraphrase: In addition to periodic Risk Reports, Anthropic will publish individual model risk analyses under specified circumstances.

context_stem: We will publish an analysis of an individual model's relevant risks in the following circumstances:
excerpt: When we publicly deploy a model that we determine is (1) significantly more capable than (2) all models for which we have publicly analyzed risks related to chemical/biological weapons production, high-stakes misalignment, or automated R&D (e.g., in a prior Risk Report, System Card, or other public artifact).
paraphrase: An off-cycle analysis is published when a publicly deployed model is judged significantly more capable than all previously publicly risk-assessed models on key threat domains.
stated_bar: significantly more capable than all models for which we have publicly analyzed risks

context_stem: We will publish an analysis of an individual model's relevant risks in the following circumstances:
excerpt: Within 30 days of determining that we have an internally deployed model that (1) could pose risks related to high-stakes misalignment or automated R&D that (2) significantly exceed those of all models for which we have publicly analyzed such risks (e.g., in a prior Risk Report, System Card, or other public artifact).
paraphrase: An off-cycle analysis is published within 30 days of determining an internal model poses materially greater misalignment or automated R&D risk than all previously publicly assessed models.
stated_bar: within 30 days; significantly exceed those of all models for which we have publicly analyzed such risks

excerpt: Several principles guide how we approach Risk Reports:
paraphrase: A set of principles governs Anthropic's approach to Risk Reports.

context_stem: Several principles guide how we approach Risk Reports:
excerpt: We intend for our Risk Reports to be direct, candid, and informative about how we see the risks of our systems and our state of preparedness for them.
paraphrase: Anthropic aims for Risk Reports to be direct, candid, and informative about risks and preparedness.

context_stem: Several principles guide how we approach Risk Reports:
excerpt: In particular, we will acknowledge when we view certain models as posing significant risks in absolute terms, even if our marginal contribution to overall ecosystem risk may be relatively limited when taking other developers’ AI models into account.
paraphrase: Anthropic will acknowledge absolute risk from its models even when its marginal contribution to ecosystem-wide risk seems limited.

context_stem: Several principles guide how we approach Risk Reports:
excerpt: We will put significant effort into investigating (for example, via capability evaluations) the case for risk, and into sharing what we find.
paraphrase: Anthropic will invest significant effort in investigating and disclosing evidence relevant to risk.

context_stem: Several principles guide how we approach Risk Reports:
excerpt: When a Risk Report describes risk mitigations we have in place (or plan to implement shortly), we will keep our future practices in line with this description or track and report noteworthy changes and deviations (generally via subsequent Risk Reports).
paraphrase: Anthropic will either maintain described mitigation practices or report noteworthy deviations from them in future Risk Reports.

context_stem: Several principles guide how we approach Risk Reports:
excerpt: We should make a strong attempt to ensure that ongoing (as opposed to temporary) changes do not significantly increase the level of risk.
paraphrase: Anthropic will strongly attempt to prevent ongoing practice changes from significantly increasing risk.

excerpt: We will describe how we identify, evaluate, and mitigate catastrophic risks.
paraphrase: Anthropic will describe its process for identifying, evaluating, and mitigating catastrophic risks.

excerpt: A Risk Report will document the following:
paraphrase: The Risk Report will document a specified set of items.

context_stem: A Risk Report will document the following (Factual information):
excerpt: Threat model identification: Our criteria for determining which catastrophic risks (i.e., threat models) we assess.
paraphrase: The report will state the criteria used to determine which catastrophic risks are assessed.

context_stem: A Risk Report will document the following (Factual information):
excerpt: Threat model specification: The relevant threat models (which will, at a minimum, include those discussed above).
paraphrase: The report will specify the relevant threat models, including at minimum those already discussed.

context_stem: A Risk Report will document the following (Factual information):
excerpt: Evidence (including evaluations) about relevant model capabilities and behaviors: For each in-scope model, capability and alignment evaluations (conducted internally and by external parties as appropriate), their results, and (as appropriate) other evidence we considered in assessing the level of risk.
paraphrase: For each in-scope model, the report will present capability and alignment evaluations, their results, and other relevant evidence considered.

context_stem: A Risk Report will document the following (Factual information):
excerpt: Risk mitigations: For each in-scope model, the mitigations we are implementing across security, deployment safeguards, and alignment domains, along with discussion of their effectiveness.
paraphrase: The report will describe mitigations implemented across security, deployment safeguards, and alignment for each in-scope model, and discuss their effectiveness.

context_stem: A Risk Report will document the following (Factual information):
excerpt: Additional relevant factors: Any other considerations material to our risk analysis.
paraphrase: The report will note any other considerations material to the risk analysis.

excerpt: We will provide our reasoning and conclusions regarding both specific threat models and overall risk levels.
paraphrase: The report will present reasoning and conclusions on specific threat models and overall risk levels.

excerpt: Threat-specific risk assessment: For each threat model, we will analyze remaining absolute risk–i.e., the leftover risk after accounting for our mitigations.
paraphrase: For each threat model, the report will analyze remaining absolute risk after mitigations.

excerpt: We will also discuss whether we believe we’ve crossed relevant thresholds in our recommendations for industry-wide safety (see Section 1), and (as relevant) whether we believe we’re meeting the risk mitigation standards corresponding to them.
paraphrase: The report will discuss whether industry-wide safety thresholds have been crossed and whether corresponding mitigation standards are being met.

excerpt: Overall risk assessment: We will provide an overall risk assessment.
paraphrase: The report will provide an overall assessment of risk.

excerpt: Risk-benefit determination: We will explain whether, and if so why, we believe the identified risks are justified by corresponding benefits.
paraphrase: The report will explain whether identified risks are justified by corresponding benefits.

excerpt: Looking forward: We will outline our plans for continuing to monitor and mitigate the relevant risks over time.
paraphrase: The report will outline ongoing plans for monitoring and mitigating relevant risks.

excerpt: Review of past Risk Reports and decisions. We will address:
paraphrase: The report will include a review of past Risk Reports and decisions.

locator: 3.3 / Review of past Risk Reports / item 1
context_stem: Review of past Risk Reports and decisions. We will address:
excerpt: Changes in risk mitigation practices—noteworthy cases in which our risk mitigation practices deviated (including temporarily) or changed from what we discussed in our previous Risk Report over the relevant period, and their implications for the overall level of risk.
paraphrase: The report will note significant deviations or changes in risk mitigation practices since the prior report and their risk implications.

locator: 3.3 / Review of past Risk Reports / item 2
context_stem: Review of past Risk Reports and decisions. We will address:
excerpt: Decisions to internally deploy in-scope models that would not otherwise be reviewed in a Risk Report (because they happened in between Risk Reports).
paraphrase: The report will cover internal deployment decisions for in-scope models that occurred between Risk Reports.

locator: 3.3 / Review of past Risk Reports / item 2
context_stem: Review of past Risk Reports and decisions. We will address:
excerpt: We will discuss how these decisions were made and whether they appear reasonable in light of any noteworthy new information that has come to light since then.
paraphrase: The report will discuss how such interim decisions were made and assess their reasonableness given new information.

locator: 3.3 / Review of past Risk Reports / item 3
context_stem: Review of past Risk Reports and decisions. We will address:
excerpt: Changes to our Frontier Safety Roadmap and any cases where we failed to meet our goals.
paraphrase: The report will note changes to the Frontier Safety Roadmap and any goal shortfalls.

excerpt: If we determine that the absolute level of risk being imposed industry-wide by AI systems such as ours is high, and are justifying our decision to move forward based partly on a marginal risk analysis, we will additionally address the following:
paraphrase: If high industry-wide absolute risk exists and the decision to proceed relies partly on marginal risk analysis, additional items will be addressed.

context_stem: We will additionally address the following (Marginal risk and ecosystem analysis):
excerpt: Competitive landscape analysis: What we know about how our current and future model capabilities and risk mitigations compare to those of relevant competitors.
paraphrase: The report will compare current and future model capabilities and mitigations to those of relevant competitors.

context_stem: We will additionally address the following (Marginal risk and ecosystem analysis):
excerpt: Role in risk assessment: How these comparisons factored into our risk assessment.
paraphrase: The report will explain how competitive comparisons informed the risk assessment.

context_stem: We will additionally address the following (Marginal risk and ecosystem analysis):
excerpt: Benefits analysis: The benefits, if any, of continuing to maintain our existing models or of advancing frontier capabilities, including considerations related to our mission and our ability to contribute to AI safety research and policy development.
paraphrase: The report will analyze benefits of maintaining or advancing frontier capabilities, including mission-related considerations.

context_stem: We will additionally address the following (Marginal risk and ecosystem analysis):
excerpt: Advocacy efforts: The steps we took to raise public awareness of the relevant risks and to encourage appropriate regulatory action, including our engagement with policymakers and other AI developers.
paraphrase: The report will describe advocacy steps taken to raise awareness and encourage regulation, including engagement with policymakers and developers.

excerpt: We will conduct the assessments above with respect to each in-scope model.
paraphrase: The described assessments will be conducted for each in-scope model.

excerpt: To avoid redundancy, we will likely analyze similar models collectively rather than individually, with appropriate justification for any such groupings.
paraphrase: Similar models may be analyzed together rather than individually, with justification, to avoid redundancy.

excerpt: Initial assessment and drafting: Our internal subject matter experts will conduct risk assessments and draft the Risk Report.
paraphrase: Internal subject matter experts conduct risk assessments and draft the Risk Report.

excerpt: Review and feedback: We will solicit comprehensive internal feedback on the report, focusing on identifying potential methodological weaknesses, analytical gaps, or areas requiring additional evidence or clarification.
paraphrase: Comprehensive internal feedback is solicited to identify weaknesses, gaps, or areas needing clarification.

excerpt: We may also use this feedback to improve or refine the report itself. We will usually also seek feedback from trusted external parties with relevant expertise.
paraphrase: Internal feedback may refine the report, and external expert feedback is usually also sought.

excerpt: Executive approval: The Risk Report, along with the internal feedback and any available external feedback, will be sent to the CEO and Responsible Scaling Officer (RSO) for final review and approval.
paraphrase: The Risk Report and associated feedback go to the CEO and RSO for final review and approval.

excerpt: The CEO and RSO will make the ultimate determination regarding the adequacy of the risk assessment and any downstream deployment or development plans.
paraphrase: The CEO and RSO have final authority over the adequacy of the risk assessment and related deployment or development plans.

excerpt: Governance notification: Following approval of a Risk Report, the CEO and RSO will promptly share their decision(s), the underlying Risk Report, and internal feedback with both the Board and the LTBT.
paraphrase: After approval, the CEO and RSO promptly share the decision, report, and internal feedback with the Board and LTBT.

excerpt: Modified process when marginal risk analysis is important to our case. In the event that marginal risk analysis (see previous section) plays a major role in a decision to move forward, explicit approval of the Risk Report by the Board and LTBT (rather than just the CEO and RSO) will be required.
paraphrase: When marginal risk analysis plays a major role in a forward decision, the Board and LTBT, not just the CEO and RSO, must explicitly approve the Risk Report.

excerpt: By “marginal risk analysis,” we mean arguing that the risks imposed by our systems in particular are relatively lower when keeping in mind the risks unavoidably posed by other AI systems.
paraphrase: Marginal risk analysis is defined as arguing Anthropic's systems pose relatively lower risk given unavoidable risks from other AI systems.

excerpt: We will publish a public version of our Risk Report. We will aim to minimize redactions to the public version of the report.
paraphrase: A public version of the Risk Report will be published, with redactions minimized.

excerpt: Reasons we may redact material include but are not limited to:
paraphrase: A non-exhaustive list of reasons for redacting material follows.

context_stem: Reasons we may redact material include but are not limited to:
excerpt: Legal compliance: To comply with legal obligations on disclosing information, such as export control regulations, national security restrictions, or contractual obligations with third parties.
paraphrase: Redactions may occur to comply with legal obligations such as export controls, national security rules, or contracts.

context_stem: Reasons we may redact material include but are not limited to:
excerpt: Intellectual property protection: To protect proprietary information, including technical details of our models and training methodologies, trade secrets, or other confidential business information.
paraphrase: Redactions may protect proprietary technical details, trade secrets, or confidential business information.

context_stem: Reasons we may redact material include but are not limited to:
excerpt: Public safety considerations: To protect public safety by not disclosing information that could be exploited to cause harm.
paraphrase: Redactions may occur to prevent disclosure of information exploitable for harm.

context_stem: Reasons we may redact material include but are not limited to:
excerpt: Privacy: To protect the personal privacy of individuals.
paraphrase: Redactions may protect individuals' personal privacy.

excerpt: We will work toward a practice of seeking comprehensive, public external review on our Risk Reports.
paraphrase: Anthropic will work toward comprehensive, public external review of Risk Reports.

excerpt: This means working with one or more third-party organizations that will receive private versions of our Risk Reports (unredacted or with minimal redactions, as discussed below) and publish comprehensive commentary on them.
paraphrase: External review involves third-party organizations receiving largely unredacted Risk Reports and publishing comprehensive commentary.

excerpt: Commentary will address topics including the quality of our reasoning, the validity of our risk assessments, the overall level of risk, and whether the redactions we’ve made for the public version are reasonable and appropriate.
paraphrase: Reviewer commentary will cover reasoning quality, risk assessment validity, overall risk level, and reasonableness of redactions.

excerpt: Our intent is for external reviewers’ judgments to carry significant weight in the eyes of the public as well as our employees.
paraphrase: Anthropic intends external reviewers' judgments to carry significant weight with the public and employees.

excerpt: But there are no well-established organizations or procedures for this sort of practice, and we are approaching it as an experiment.
paraphrase: Anthropic acknowledges no established organizations or procedures exist yet, treating this as an experimental practice.

excerpt: At a minimum, we will complete a full external review process (described below) with at least one external reviewer anytime a Risk Report covers highly capable models and is significantly redacted, defined as follows:
paraphrase: A full external review with at least one reviewer is required whenever a Risk Report covers highly capable models and is significantly redacted, per the definitions given.
stated_bar: highly capable models and significantly redacted

excerpt: A model is “highly capable” if we conclude that it crosses the threshold for automated AI R&D described in Section 1.
paraphrase: A model is deemed highly capable if it crosses the automated AI R&D threshold defined in Section 1.
stated_bar: crosses the threshold for automated AI R&D described in Section 1

excerpt: “Significantly redacted” means that the redactions omit information a reasonable external safety researcher would consider important in evaluating the overall level of risk, such that a reader of only the public version could not meaningfully assess whether they agree with our conclusions.
paraphrase: Significantly redacted means omissions of information a reasonable safety researcher would deem important, preventing meaningful assessment from the public version alone.

excerpt: A report shall be deemed significantly redacted if, in the judgment of the RSO, CEO, Board, or LTBT, it meets this description.
paraphrase: The RSO, CEO, Board, or LTBT can determine that a report is significantly redacted based on their judgment.

excerpt: Note that unredacted reports will be shared with a large number of employees, who will be in a position to raise concerns if they believe the public version meets this description.
paraphrase: Unredacted reports are shared broadly with employees, enabling them to raise concerns about excessive redaction.

excerpt: In addition, upon the LTBT’s request, we will conduct a public or private external review of our Risk Report or sections thereof, subject to the procedures outlined below.
paraphrase: Upon LTBT request, a public or private external review of the Risk Report or parts thereof will be conducted, per the outlined procedures.

excerpt: We will select external reviewers that:
paraphrase: Criteria follow for selecting external reviewers.

context_stem: We will select external reviewers that:
excerpt: Have significant experience and expertise regarding evaluations for dangerous AI capabilities and propensities. It’s particularly important that they be knowledgeable about potential ways such evaluations might be misleading (for example, alignment faking).
paraphrase: Reviewers must have significant expertise in dangerous capability evaluations and understand ways such evaluations can mislead, such as alignment faking.

context_stem: We will select external reviewers that:
excerpt: Have reputational and other incentives making them likely to be candid about their assessment of risks, rather than focused on writing comments that Anthropic will approve of.
paraphrase: Reviewers should have incentives favoring candor over pleasing Anthropic.

context_stem: We will select external reviewers that:
excerpt: For example, external review parties should not be teams whose revenue, reputation and success depend entirely on Anthropic and similar companies continuing to work with them.
paraphrase: Reviewers should not depend entirely on Anthropic and similar companies for revenue, reputation, or success.

context_stem: We will select external reviewers that:
excerpt: Do not have conflicts of interest with respect to Anthropic. At a minimum, a reviewing organization itself may not have a financial interest in Anthropic;
paraphrase: Reviewers must lack conflicts of interest; at minimum, the reviewing organization itself may not hold a financial interest in Anthropic.

context_stem: We will select external reviewers that:
excerpt: and the individuals involved in conducting the review, as well as anyone above them in the reporting chain within their organization, may not have a financial interest in Anthropic or close personal relationships with anyone at Anthropic (i.e., family relationships, romantic relationships, or shared living arrangements).
paraphrase: Individuals conducting the review and their superiors may not hold financial interests in Anthropic or close personal relationships with Anthropic staff.

excerpt: In selecting external reviewers, we will consult with the Board and obtain the approval of the LTBT.
paraphrase: Selection of external reviewers requires Board consultation and LTBT approval.

excerpt: The external review process will involve sharing the Risk Report with one or more external reviewers within one week of submitting the same report to our Board and LTBT.
paraphrase: External reviewers receive the Risk Report within one week of its submission to the Board and LTBT.

excerpt: We will ask the external reviewers to provide public commentary on our report within 30 days of receipt.
paraphrase: External reviewers are asked to provide public commentary within 30 days of receiving the report.

excerpt: We will try to work toward a process that involves the full external review being completed prior to Board/LTBT review (and may require this later).
paraphrase: Anthropic will work toward completing full external review before Board/LTBT review, possibly making this mandatory later.

excerpt: For purposes of external review, the only redactions to the Risk Report will be those necessary to comply with legal prohibitions or to maintain our legal rights.
paraphrase: For external review purposes, redactions are limited to those legally necessary.

excerpt: We expect that we will also invest some time in answering follow-up questions from parties doing external review.
paraphrase: Anthropic expects to spend time answering follow-up questions from external reviewers.

excerpt: For example, we may redact information if sharing it would endanger our legal right to treat it as confidential. This would be an uncommon situation.
paraphrase: Redaction may occur if disclosure would endanger legal confidentiality rights, though this would be uncommon.

excerpt: It does not mean we would redact information merely because it is sensitive or to reduce the risk of a leak.
paraphrase: Sensitivity alone or leak-risk reduction does not justify redaction.

excerpt: The external review will address:
paraphrase: The following topics will be covered by the external review.

excerpt: Adequacy of information: Whether the Risk Report contains sufficient information to assess the identified risks;
paraphrase: The review assesses whether the Risk Report has enough information to evaluate identified risks.

excerpt: Analytical rigor: The strength of the Risk Report’s reasoning and analysis;
paraphrase: The review evaluates the strength of the report's reasoning and analysis.

excerpt: Areas of disagreement: Whether the external reviewer disagrees with any of the Risk Report’s key claims and, if so, the reasons for any such disagreements; and
paraphrase: The review notes any disagreements with the report's key claims and the reasons for them.

excerpt: Risk reduction recommendations: Recommendations for further reducing identified risks.
paraphrase: The review provides recommendations for further reducing identified risks.

excerpt: The external reviewer will also evaluate our redaction decisions while avoiding disclosure of the redacted content itself.
paraphrase: The reviewer evaluates redaction decisions without disclosing the redacted content.

excerpt: In particular, the review will cover:
paraphrase: The review covers specific redaction-related topics.

context_stem: In particular, the review will cover:
excerpt: Redaction scope: The general nature and scope of redactions;
paraphrase: The review addresses the general nature and scope of redactions.

context_stem: In particular, the review will cover:
excerpt: Redaction justification: Whether the external reviewer generally agrees or disagrees with the publicly stated reasons for the redactions and, if relevant, the reasons for any disagreements;
paraphrase: The review addresses reviewer agreement or disagreement with stated redaction justifications.

context_stem: In particular, the review will cover:
excerpt: Balancing test: Whether the redactions strike a reasonable balance between Anthropic’s legitimate interests and society’s interest in transparency; and
paraphrase: The review assesses whether redactions balance Anthropic's interests against societal transparency interests.

context_stem: In particular, the review will cover:
excerpt: Materiality: Whether any of the redactions in the public report are material to any of the external reviewer’s substantive disagreements with the report’s claims.
paraphrase: The review assesses whether redactions are material to the reviewer's substantive disagreements with the report.

excerpt: We will ask the external reviewer to memorialize its findings on the topics above in a written report that is made public.
paraphrase: External reviewers are asked to document findings in a written report that is published.

excerpt: External reviewers will be bound by obligations not to disclose confidential information (e.g., confidential intellectual property, matters of national security, or proprietary details such as model architecture, cost, or size), but beyond that will not be restricted in what they can publish, including concerns about the Risk Report or Anthropic’s conduct in connection with the external review.
paraphrase: External reviewers must keep specified confidential information private but otherwise face no restriction on publishing, including criticisms of the report or Anthropic's conduct.
